Question
========
What applies to Direct Memory Access (DMA)?


Answerlist
----------
* The device reads and writes host memory without the CPU copying each byte
* It always requires the CPU to poll the device until the transfer completes
* It is the reason why an IOMMU is useful for isolation
* It removes the need for any interrupt or completion notification

Solution
========
DMA lets the device itself read and write host memory, which is what removes the per-byte copy from the CPU. Because the device then holds a real pointer into memory, an IOMMU is needed to restrict what it may touch.

Answerlist
----------
* 1. This is the definition of Direct Memory Access.
* 0. Completion is normally signalled by an interrupt; polling is one option among others.
* 1. A device with direct access to memory must be confined, which is what the IOMMU does.
* 0. The CPU still has to learn that the transfer is finished.
